title: Windowed provenance eraser for analytics events with grace-period attestations
creator: Maya Chen
description: Goal: Implement a windowed provenance-aware eraser for analytics event stores that supports a configurable grace period, cryptographically auditable attestations of deletion, and reversible proof artifacts for internal compliance review. Background: current deletion jobs remove raw events but lack provenance scoping, grace-period handling for queued downstream exports, and an attestation export that legal/compliance can consume. This ticket builds the eraser service, a reconciliation job that validates deletions against provenance tokens, and the attestation export pipeline. Success metrics: (1) all configured retention-policy deletions (by dataset/namespace) complete within SLA, (2) attestations generated for 100% of retention runs, (3) zero missing provenance false-positives in reconciliation tests, (4) integration tests + canary run on 20% of prod traffic without customer-impact incidents.
acceptance_criteria: Eraser service removes events within the configured window and marks provenance tokens as 'erased' in provenance index
Grace-period behavior: events in 'pending export' state are queued for deferred deletion until downstream ACK or expiry; deletion must not occur while exports are in-flight
Attestation export: protocol-buffer attestation file generated per-run and uploaded to internal S3 path with checksum and signed metadata
Reconciliation job cross-checks event counts and provenance tokens, emits an automated discrepancy alert if >0.1% mismatch
All new DB schema changes have migrations and rollback plan, with minimal lock time (<30s) on critical tables
Runbook updated with steps to re-run erasure for a given provenance-token range and to revoke attestations in case of false deletion
implementation_notes: Introduce a provenance_index table (provenance_token, dataset, event_count, status, last_updated) — status in {active, pending, erased}
Eraser service components: coordinator (kubernetes cronjob), worker pool (k8s job), and reconciliation lambda for cross-region validation
Grace period state machine: active -> pending_export -> export_acknowledged -> tombstone -> erased. Transition events emitted to audit log stream
Use HMAC-signed attestations (service key from KMS) rather than plaintext CSVs to avoid tamper risk. Include run_id, dataset, token_range, delete_count, timestamp
Deletion should prefer soft-delete tombstones first; physical purge happens in a separate retention sweep after attestations are generated and retention window elapses
Telemetry: emit token-level metrics (deleted_count, reconciliation_mismatch, delete_latency) to observability with retention 90 days for troubleshooting
migration_plan: Phase 1: Add provenance_index table with default status=active; backfill provenance tokens for last 90 days via streaming job (low-priority). Use online batching to avoid DB contention
Phase 2: Deploy eraser coordinator in canary region; run in dry-run mode (no physical deletes) for 72 hours and compare to baseline deletion job results
Phase 3: Enable tombstone marking for canary dataset (20% of datasets), generate attestations but do not physically purge until QA signoff
Phase 4: Full rollout with phased increase of dataset coverage and final physical purge sweep after attestations are archived
Rollback: if reconciliation mismatch > threshold, pause coordinator and run compensating job to rehydrate tombstones; legal to be notified automatically
testing_plan: Unit tests for state transitions and attestation generation (100% coverage for core modules),
Integration test harness that spins up ephemeral event store, simulates downstream export delays, and asserts grace-period semantics
Reconciliation fuzz tests with injected mismatches to validate alerting path
Performance test: end-to-end deletion throughput at target batch sizes (benchmark vs. current job)
Canary validation: 72h dry-run comparison against historical deletes; discrepancy tolerance <0.05%
rollout_plan: Deploy coordinator in staging and run full workflow against staging analytics data
Canary region dag run (dry-run) for 72 hours; cross-team review with Legal and Privacy
Enable tombstone marking for 20% production datasets, monitoring metrics and reconciliation alerts closely
After 1 week of stable canary, enable attestation export and schedule physical purge after configured retention window
Post-deploy: 2-week monitoring window, then expand to 100% coverage if no incidents
